builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache
summary: This method replaces the BF16 key-value cache typically used by the draft model in speculative decoding with a quantized 4-bit cache (K4V4) using per-channel keys and per-token values. The cost is a negligible drop in mean acceptance rate (less than 1.4% relative), while significantly reducing VRAM overhead. Failure can occur if the quantizer layout is not co-designed with the bit-split; naive per-token quantization of keys causes severe acceptance degradation compared to the proposed grouped per-channel approach.
rationale: It directly addresses the memory constraints of a 24GB GPU by eliminating the draft model's cache overhead in speculative decoding with negligible impact on generation throughput.
technique: Quantized Draft KV Cache in Speculative Decoding

claims.statement: This method replaces the BF16 key-value cache typically used by the draft model in speculative decoding with a quantized 4-bit cache (K4V4) using per-channel keys and per-token values. The cost is a negligible drop in mean acceptance rate (less than 1.4% relative), while significantly reducing VRAM overhead. Failure can occur if the quantizer layout is not co-designed with the bit-split; naive per-token quantization of keys causes severe acceptance degradation compared to the proposed grouped per-channel approach.
Reduces draft cache memory by 66.20% and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%, with mean acceptance dropping from 57.93% to 57.14% (1.36% relative).
